name: Imperial Beach
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Imperial Beach, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Imperial Beach, CA: Small Town Holiday at Pier Plaza with Santa photos, crafts, air jumps and a tree lighting by the pier.
lede: Imperial Beach celebrates Christmas by the ocean, with a Small Town Holiday afternoon and a tree lighting at Pier Plaza at the foot of the city's wooden pier.
celebrates: The City of Imperial Beach counts Small Town Holiday and Holiday Tree Lighting among its annual signature events, run by the Parks and Recreation department. It takes place at Portwood Pier Plaza on Seacoast Drive, where the town's pier meets the beach. Families come for photos with Santa, holiday crafts, air jumps, holiday treats and holiday lights, and the afternoon ends with a countdown and the lighting of the community tree. The city promotes it on its own pages and social accounts as a free event for all ages, and it serves as the town's kickoff to the holiday season.
lastyear: In 2025 the city held Small Town Holiday on Saturday, December 6, from 3 to 6 pm at Pier Plaza. The city called it a free, family-friendly holiday event with live holiday music, cocoa and cookies, holiday characters and a special appearance by Santa. The evening ended with a countdown to the holiday tree lighting at Pier Plaza. The city thanked sponsors including San Diego Community Power and Wyyerd Fiber.
facts: Imperial Beach was founded in 1887 and took its name from Imperial County, the desert county about 100 miles to the east. It became a city in 1956, the tenth city in San Diego County, and it is the most southwesterly city in the continental United States. The 1,500-foot wooden Imperial Beach Pier is the focal point of town, and the holiday tree goes up at the plaza at its base.
trains: Imperial Beach has no train station of its own, but the San Diego Trolley is close. MTS bus routes 933 and 934 loop through Imperial Beach from the Iris Avenue Transit Center, a stop on the Blue Line. From there the Blue Line runs north toward National City, where the 1882 National City Depot is open as a railroad museum on weekends, and on into downtown San Diego. Balboa Park's San Diego Model Railroad Museum makes a good indoor train stop on the same day.

kidfact: Imperial Beach is the most southwesterly city in the whole continental United States, so its Christmas tree stands about as far southwest as you can go.
faq: Where is the Imperial Beach tree lighting?

The City of Imperial Beach lights its holiday tree at Portwood Pier Plaza, 940 Seacoast Drive, next to the Imperial Beach Pier. The lighting closes the Small Town Holiday afternoon, which the Parks and Recreation department runs each December with Santa photos, holiday crafts and air jumps.
Is Small Town Holiday in Imperial Beach free?

Yes. The City of Imperial Beach describes Small Town Holiday as a free, family-friendly event, and its 2026 post says all ages are welcome. Photos with Santa, holiday crafts, air jumps and holiday treats are all listed as part of the afternoon, which ends with the tree lighting at the pier plaza.
Who organizes Christmas events in Imperial Beach?

The City of Imperial Beach Parks and Recreation department runs Small Town Holiday and the tree lighting as one of its annual signature events. The city lists the event on its website and calendar, and it posts updates on its own Instagram and Facebook accounts.
How do I get to Imperial Beach by trolley?

Take the San Diego Trolley Blue Line to the Iris Avenue Transit Center. MTS bus routes 933 and 934 loop through Imperial Beach from there, running along Imperial Beach Boulevard and Palm Avenue. That makes it possible to pair a trolley ride with a visit to the pier.
